definition: In the fields of computer vision and image analysis, the scale-invariant feature operator (or SFOP) is an algorithm to detect local features in images.
details: The algorithm was published by Förstner et al. in 2009.

explainer.lead: The scale-invariant feature operator (SFOP) is an algorithm for detecting local features in images, used in computer vision and image analysis. It matters because reliable local features are the building blocks for matching and analysing images across changes in scale.

tiers.eli5: It's a way of picking out distinctive spots in a picture, like corners of a building, that stay recognisable even if the picture is made bigger or smaller.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use SFOP to find repeatable keypoints for tasks like matching images taken at different scales. A pitfall is expecting detections to stay stable under changes the detector was not designed to handle.
tiers.paperLevel: It is defined as a scale-invariant local feature detector, published by Förstner et al. in 2009. As with any feature detector, its reliability depends on image content and the transformations present.

explainer.example: Two photos of the same building taken from different distances can be matched by pairing the distinctive points SFOP detects in each.
